ai.title: Remove getRequestContext from agent runtime
ai.summary: Refactored `run-agent-step.ts`, `run-programmatic-step.ts`, `web-search.ts`, and `tool-executor.ts` to accept `repoId` and `repoUrl` as explicit parameters instead of fetching them via `getRequestContext()`. This decouples tool execution from the WebSocket request context, preventing context leakage in non-WS environments like evals. `websocket-action.ts` now injects these values from the context before calling the agent loop. Updated `CodebuffToolHandlerFunction` type in `agent-runtime` to reflect the new required fields.

eli5.text: The agent no longer looks up repository information by reaching into a shared request context that can leak between environments. Instead, the repository ID and URL are now passed in explicitly as parameters wherever they are needed. You would not see a visible difference in features, but this keeps automated evaluation runs isolated from live chat sessions and prevents repository identity from bleeding across unrelated runs. It is live today.

eli5.text: A bit of clutter was cleared out of the team's automated test suite. The engineers deleted a small check that was confirming something already covered elsewhere, leaving the rest of the testing setup untouched. Since only internal tests changed and no app features were altered, you wouldn't see any difference when using the product.

Nothing you do changes today, but the codebase is now tidier and that helper is one step closer to being reused by other agent setups.

eli5.text: When an AI agent attempts a coding task and runs into trouble, this change lets the system generate a short written analysis explaining what went wrong and what the agent should have done instead. You can turn this analysis generation on or off with a new toggle, and when enabled, the system saves these write-ups into a designated folder instead of cluttering the debug logs. The system now also stops saving certain noisy error messages (those involving malformed JSON from tool calls) to reduce clutter. This is already live in the internal eval tooling used by the engineering team, so if you run a buffbench evaluation you may notice the new output folder and cleaner debug logs.

It is not visible in the app today and does nothing for users; it lives only in the codebase to help the developers who write automated assistant tools learn from past mistakes. The guide collects real failures from previous runs (such as a scrollbar that looked wrong in Firefox, tests that broke when text changed, and tools receiving unclean data) and pairs each failure with a concrete fix the assistants should follow next time. If you opened the project files, you would see a 1627-line notes file written in plain headings and bullet points, added on October 21, with no changes to anything you use.

eli5.text: The engine that powers the assistant's step-by-step reasoning was relocated into a shared runtime package, so the main application and evaluation tools now pull it from that central location instead of a local module. This is behind-the-scenes reorganization that cleans up how the system starts up and runs, removing tangled dependencies between parts of the code. If you were watching how the assistant boots up, you'd see it loading the same reasoning step from a shared toolkit rather than from inside the main application itself. It's live today as part of the normal startup flow.

ai.title: Move templates README to agent-runtime
ai.summary: Relocated `templates/README.md` from `backend/src` to `packages/agent-runtime/src`. This aligns documentation with the agent-runtime package structure. Scope limited to internal file organization; no functional code changes.

eli5.text: The guide that explains how the agent templates work has been moved into the agent-runtime section of the project, so it now sits next to the code it describes instead of being stored separately in the old backend folder. You, as someone using or reading the templates, won't notice any difference in how things work - the templates still do exactly what they did before. Only developers looking for the README file would see it in a new location, making it easier for them to find documentation close to the relevant code.

ai.title: Move main-prompt to agent-runtime package
ai.summary: Relocates `main-prompt.ts` and `check-terminal-command.ts` from `backend/src` to `packages/agent-runtime/src`. Updates imports in `websocket-action.ts` to use `@codebuff/agent-runtime/main-prompt`. Adjusts internal relative imports within the moved files to resolve dependencies correctly in the new package structure.

eli5.text: The part of the system that builds the assistant's opening reply was moved into a shared library that other tools can reuse, so future additions to the assistant can lean on the same setup instead of duplicating it. You wouldn't notice anything different today since the behavior stayed the same, but the change makes it easier to keep the assistant's instructions consistent if the team adds new features later.

ai.title: Lazy agent runtime impl in WebSocketMiddleware
ai.summary: WebSocketMiddleware now accepts Source<AgentRuntimeDeps> instead of eager AgentRuntimeDeps. getImpl() resolves function or promise sources on first use, caching result. Covers backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts. protec singleton passes BACKEND_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL as thunk to defer initialization.

eli5.text: When you connect to the assistant over a WebSocket, the system no longer has to finish loading the assistant's internals before it can respond to you; instead, it waits until your message actually arrives to start loading, then reuses that loaded setup for everything that follows in your session. This affects everyone using the WebSocket-powered assistant endpoint, and it means the very first message you send might take a touch longer while the assistant gets ready, after which subsequent messages reuse the already-loaded setup instead of reloading it again. The lazy loading and caching are in place and wired into the WebSocket middleware today.

ai.title: Add compare-buffbench-runs script for paired evaluation analysis
ai.summary: New `scripts/compare-buffbench-runs.ts` compares buffbench evaluation runs by intersecting commit SHAs. It filters out tasks with agent errors or scores <= 1.0 to ensure valid comparisons. The script outputs aggregate stats (mean, min, max, stdDev) and head-to-head deltas for score, cost, and duration across paired runs.

eli5.text: A new helper script is now available so the team can take two sets of AI-coding-assistant test results and automatically line up the tasks both runs attempted, then print side-by-side numbers for overall score, cost, and time. When you run it, you hand it two folders of result files, and it quietly skips any task where one run crashed or scored at or below 1.0 before showing mean, min, max, and spread for each assistant and the head-to-head deltas. The script is in the repository today, so anyone running BuffBench comparisons can start using it immediately; no existing workflows change, and nothing currently depends on it except people doing these paired evaluations.

ai.title: Update base2-gpt-5 worker agent configuration
ai.summary: Replaced `reviewer-gpt-5` with `code-reviewer-gpt-5` and `validator-gpt-5` in `base2-gpt-5-worker.ts`. Updated workflow steps to separate code review from validation commands. Adjusted `main-single-eval.ts` and `main.ts` to use `base2-max` agent.

eli5.text: The assistant that writes code now separates checking the work from making sure it's correct - one step reviews the code itself, and a separate step runs tests and type checks. The set of helper tools it can call during reviews also changed names, and the example projects it runs were pointed at a more capable setup. This is live today for anyone running these internal evaluation tasks.

ai.title: Add base2-max, planner-pro prompt, buffbench agents
ai.summary: Added base2-max.ts and expanded createBase2 to support fast, normal, and max modes. Planner-pro spawnerPrompt updated to 'Uses deep thinking to generate an implementation plan for a user request.'. Eval buffbench/main.ts agents changed to base2-fast, base2, base-max with taskConcurrency set to 10. Files: .agents/base2/base2-max.ts, .agents/base2/base2.ts, .agents/planners/planner-pro.ts, evals/buffbench/main.ts.

eli5.text: The system now offers three strength levels for its main helper: a quick-and-light version for fast answers, the standard version you were already using, and a new power version that brings in an extra specialist agent to tackle harder jobs. If you look behind the scenes, the quick version still skips a couple of check-in steps, the standard version works as before, and the power version activates an additional worker alongside the usual reviewers. The internal tester that judges how these helpers perform has also been switched to run these three versions side by side, with each version handling up to ten jobs at once instead of the old setup.

ai.title: Remove base2 agent variants
ai.summary: Deleted .agents/base2/base2-code-reviewer.ts, base2-no-review.ts, base2-simple.ts, and base2-validator.ts. These files defined experimental 'Buffy' orchestrator variants with specific sub-agent spawn configurations. This internal cleanup removes deprecated agent definitions from the repository.

eli5.text: The engineers removed four experimental helper versions of their main coding assistant, named after the character 'Buffy,' that were used to test different ways the assistant could organize its work. These four variants, designed for different review, simple, and validation workflows, are no longer part of the project. If you browsed the repository today, you would not find the folders or files that defined these test configurations, since they have been permanently deleted from the codebase. This is an internal cleanup and does not change the behavior of the assistant you interact with.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant in your terminal, the status messages and error notes it prints out now follow a single, consistent layout instead of mixing different formats from different parts of the app. Behind the scenes, the terminal interface switched its logging system to match a shared format already used by the rest of the application, so messages like 'Failed to copy to clipboard' or 'Starting mock response streaming' display their extra details (such as the prompt or theme name) in the same structured way everywhere. The assistant now logs errors and info with the context details first, then the human-readable message, making troubleshooting output easier to read whether the error came from copying text, sending a message, or detecting your system's light/dark theme. This is live

ai.title: Add base2-fast-schooled agent with 50% lesson compression
ai.summary: New `base2-fast-schooled.ts` defines `Buffy the Schooled Orchestrator`, inheriting `fast` base config but injecting compressed historical lessons into system prompts. This variant targets eval benchmarks in `evals/buffbench/main.ts`, reducing prompt token overhead by retaining only half of accumulated agent failure patterns compared to the standard schooled agent. Scope limited to internal eval infrastructure and agent definition files; no user-facing CLI or Web changes.

eli5.text: A new internal test helper for the company's coding assistant has been added and switched on in the evaluation suite as of October 21, 2025. This helper is a faster version of an existing learning assistant, but it deliberately keeps only half of the past mistakes it has collected, so its suggestions are built from a shortened history. The change is live for internal testing only and does not change anything visible to users of the product.
